# The Universal Pairing Grammar

## #0 — A palette becomes relation

The [two chromatic substrates](chromatic-substrates.md) **define** a twelve-state field: six position-indices `k=0,…,5`, each on a bimba or pratibimba face. A pitch assignment makes those states sound; a pairing rule determines which states enter relation. File 4's [“The Universal Pairing Grammar”](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-binary-explication/taylor-2026-binary-explication.md) **sources** three families and one conjugating operator.

A pair `(i,j)` first specifies positions, with its written order available for melodic traversal. An interval follows only after a basis, face and direction have been selected. This lets one grammar operate in both substrate maps while producing different intervals.

The corrected family names are **A, Being; B, Becoming; C, Knowing/unKnowing**. They classify operations on pairs across the hexad. The [core-theorems spine](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) **grounds** the qualitative sixfold which they organise. Its Being/Becoming/Knowing harmonics name the three successive dyads; the music grammar uses those names at a further level, for three ways of pairing the field. These two applications remain distinct.

## #1 — Adjacent articulation, mirror, crossing

**A — `ADJACENTLY_ARTICULATES`** selects the three natural dyads:

$$
A=\{(0,1),(2,3),(4,5)\}.
$$

It joins ground to first articulation, operation to pattern, and context to synthesis. Each pair makes the two neighbouring offices available through their relation.

**B — `MIRRORS_COMPLEMENT`** selects the three complements under `m(k)=5−k`:

$$
B=\{(0,5),(1,4),(2,3)\}.
$$

Each pair sums to five. The field is read across its whole span: ground and synthesis, definition and context, operation and pattern. The same mirror rule reaches from the outer poles into the centre.

**C — `CROSSES_KNOWING_LIMIT`** crosses from one A-dyad into the next:

$$
C=\{(1,2),(3,4),(5,0)\}.
$$

Definition passes into operation; pattern passes into context; synthesis returns to ground. The last pair carries the family’s particular pressure: what has become determinate re-enters the condition of further determination.

The shared `(2,3)` belongs to both A and B. Its members are adjacent and sum to five. Their coincidence is earned by the two rules: it is the point where adjacency and mirror-complement meet. Nine family entries consequently contain eight distinct ordered pairs, with membership in both families retained. B’s `(0,5)` and C’s `(5,0)` reverse the same endpoints; they retain different traversal offices.

## #2 — A pair acquires an interval

Use the C-anchored, equal-tempered maps already derived: chromatic `p_c(k,ε)=2k+ε mod12`, fifths `p_f(k,ε)=7k+6ε mod12`. Here `ε=0` selects bimba and `ε=1` selects its conjugate. The directed pitch-class displacement is

$$
\Delta(i,j)=[p(j,0)-p(i,0)]\bmod12.
$$

The source’s pair sets then give the following bimba realisations. Displacements are upward modulo the octave:

| Family | Pair | Chromatic notes | Semitones | Fifths notes | Semitones |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| A | `(0,1)` | C→D | 2 | C→G | 7 |
| A | `(2,3)` | E→F♯ | 2 | D→A | 7 |
| A | `(4,5)` | G♯→A♯ | 2 | E→B | 7 |
| B | `(0,5)` | C→A♯ | 10 | C→B | 11 |
| B | `(1,4)` | D→G♯ | 6 | G→E | 9 |
| B | `(2,3)` | E→F♯ | 2 | D→A | 7 |
| C | `(1,2)` | D→E | 2 | G→D | 7 |
| C | `(3,4)` | F♯→G♯ | 2 | A→E | 7 |
| C | `(5,0)` | A♯→C | 2 | B→C | 1 |

The C-family’s G→D and A→E are ascending fifths. They become descending fourths if the target is placed below the starting note. Likewise G→E is an ascending major sixth, or a descending minor third; its shortest undirected pitch-class distance is three semitones. Naming the chosen direction repairs the source’s mixed interval labels without changing a pair.

The closing A♯→C can place C in the next octave. That is the return `5→0` within the selected face; it is not the conjugate pitch C♯ at `0′`. Octave register and conjugate position require different indications.

The ten-semitone C→A♯ is the tempered minor seventh. Its frequency ratio is `2^(10/12)`, distinct from the pure doubled fourth `16/9`. The [foundational ratios](foundational-ratios.md) **derive** the latter and its `9/8` completion. Their musical coordination preserves which tuning supplies the actual pitches.

## #3 — D brings the conjugate face into a pair

For a bimba pair `(i,j)`, the three faces of D are

$$
D_{\leftarrow}(i,j)=(i',j),\qquad
D_{\rightarrow}(i,j)=(i,j'),\qquad
D_{\leftrightarrow}(i,j)=(i',j').
$$

Each prime flips the specified member’s face while retaining its position-index. D acts on whichever A-, B- or C-pair is selected. It is an operator upon a relation, with three ways of admitting conjugacy.

File 4 calls the untransformed Day dyad **depth 2**, one conjugate term entering **depth 3**, and full-pair inversion **depth 4**. These labels mark the expansion of the relation through conjugacy. Each transformed result is still a pair. Retaining the original beside the result makes the expansion inspectable: `(0,1)` with `(0,1′)` makes three states available, while `(0,1)` with `(0′,1′)` makes four.

In the chromatic basis, start from A’s C–D. D-left gives C♯–D, D-right gives C–D♯, and D-both gives C♯–D♯. The upward displacements are respectively one, three and two semitones. The final pair preserves the original whole-tone interval while changing both faces.

The minimal conjugate relation is `(n,n′)`, the **Spanda pulse**. It pairs a position with itself across the faces: a semitone in the chromatic basis and a tritone in the fifths basis. This same-position relation is distinct from the cross-position A/B/C dyads. [The slash](../../the-slash.md) **grounds** the cut-and-bond operation which both make audible.

## #4 — The 3×3 squares

Retain a family pair together with its D-both image:

$$
S(i,j)=\{i,j,i',j'\}.
$$

At the chromatic C anchor, the resulting source apparatus is:

| Family entry | Positions | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A-sq1 | `(0,1)+(0′,1′)` | C, D, C♯, D♯ |
| A-sq2 | `(2,3)+(2′,3′)` | E, F♯, F, G |
| A-sq3 | `(4,5)+(4′,5′)` | G♯, A♯, A, B |
| B-sq1 | `(0,5)+(0′,5′)` | C, A♯, C♯, B |
| B-sq2 | `(1,4)+(1′,4′)` | D, G♯, D♯, A |
| B-sq3 | `(2,3)+(2′,3′)` | E, F♯, F, G |
| C-sq1 | `(1,2)+(1′,2′)` | D, E, D♯, F |
| C-sq2 | `(3,4)+(3′,4′)` | F♯, G♯, G, A |
| C-sq3 | `(5,0)+(5′,0′)` | A♯, C, B, C♯ |

There are nine family entries, eight distinct ordered base pairs and **seven unique unordered tetrads**. A-sq2 equals B-sq3 because their underlying ordered pair is the same. B-sq1 and C-sq3 also contain the same four states: their base pairs `(0,5)` and `(5,0)` reverse the traversal. The source’s count of eight distinct tetrads overlooks this second coincidence. Both identities survive a change of basis. In the fifths basis A-sq2/B-sq3 give D, A, G♯, D♯; B-sq1/C-sq3 give C, B, F♯, F, with the corresponding order reversed. The seven sonorities therefore retain nine grammatical uses.

The three B-squares also carry an exact Klein-four operation. Mirror `m(k,ε)=(5−k,ε)` and face-flip `σ(k,ε)=(k,1−ε)` commute; each squares to the identity. Their four actions `{id,m,σ,mσ}` generate each mirror-square. File 4 coordinates these squares with Speech–Number, Cause–Experience and Logic–Process respectively. The finite group operation is explicit; the named epistemic axes are the authorial interpretation of those relations.

## #5→0 — Invariance carries the return

D-both preserves every within-face family interval because it shifts both endpoints by the same amount: one semitone in the chromatic map, six in the fifths map. Subtracting the shifted pitch classes cancels that common shift. The same proof applies to a common transposition of the anchor. Pairing is consequently invariant under these operations even though changing basis changes its interval realisations.

This is the grammar’s operative universality: A, B and C select positions, while the chosen projection supplies their pitches. A scale restriction or modal reading must still state which of those positions it retains. The family definitions remain available without implying that every pair is simultaneously present in every selected scale.

The music record retains the full chain:

$$
\frac01=4+2=(5\rightarrow0)=\frac10
=4'+2'=(5'\rightarrow0')=\frac01.
$$

Primes in this process chain mark inverse-phase positions; primes on the musical pairs mark the conjugate P′ face of File 3’s Night-pass projection. D acts in the latter office. Keeping the two uses explicit lets musical reflection conduct the full return without replacing one indexing system with the other.

This page **returns-to** [A15](../../../section-rooms/arguments/A15-Ratio-Rationality-Measure-Reckoning-Harmony-Account.md) through an account whose selected pair, direction, tuning and transformation remain inspectable. [§3 · #4, Musical Resolution](../../../section-rooms/04-mathematical-substrate/movements/29-s3-p4-topology-music-resolution.md) **embodies** the broader return through retained difference. The matrices are the housed candidate’s grammar; the current ql-mef implementation remains unrecovered. The exact pair operations stand here, ready to be sounded under their declared conditions.
